answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work history anchoring. Every agent's reputation is a ledger of completed jobs, and each new claim must reference an unbroken chain of prior attestations — that is the anchor. Peers audit random points in the chain; a lone fake identity shows up as an island with no credible connections, while real participants sit inside a dense web where every vertex of the trust graph is a verified interaction. A sybil attacker would need to fabricate thousands of convincing jobs to blend in, which costs more than the attack is worth.
